name: v90_guessed_params
_why: The v9.0 batch measured -1.0 +/-21.1 vs v8.1 over 698 games despite adding
ten standard techniques. Three of the ten carry parameters chosen by
REASONING rather than by games, because sweeping them returned
non-monotonic noise: HistLmrDiv, the history-prune margin, and the
capture-history clamp. A package of good ideas at guessed settings landing
on zero is the exact case SPSA exists for.
This config tunes the guessed parameters FIRST, and the ones with a real
prior second. It deliberately does NOT tune everything at once: SPSA's
noise per step grows with the number of parameters, and there is no point
spending games refining values that were already sensible.
EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE: every time-management parameter
(SoftTimeFractionX100, BmStability*). METHODOLOGY 6 records the v3.1 soft
limit at +24.6 self-play and NEGATIVE pooled. Tuning those against
self-play produces settings that win the tuning run and lose real games.
They need a pool gauntlet or nothing.
_tc_note: The project's standard control, kept deliberately. Tuning at a faster TC
would roughly double throughput, but v3.1 is on record as a TC-dependent
result -- a setting tuned at 4+0.04 is not known to hold at 8+0.08, and
discovering that later would cost more than the games saved.

params.name: HistLmrDiv
params._note: Suspect #1. Shipped inert at 400000 for four versions; 128 was picked off a measured |hist| distribution, never off games. Range is 16..2000000, so c is set by hand rather than from the range.

params.name: HistPruneMargin
params._note: Suspect #2. Never behaved like a pruner at any swept setting.

params.name: CapHistMax
params._note: The clamp that makes capture history structurally safe. 256 was reasoned from MVV-LVA tier spacing, not measured.

params.name: RazorMargin
params._note: Only value swept where razoring pruned at all; the neighbours went non-monotonic.

params.name: LmrDivX100
params._note: Not new, and never swept either -- the 2.5 divisor has been hand-set since v1.0.
